X.note: The painted portrait on a tilted mat looks good, and the warm red backdrop gives strong contrast and a focal point. The caption is clear. The source line is small, grey and low-contrast on a phone. The mat bleeds into the gradient behind the text, which looks slightly muddy. The text sits far from the image, and the gap between the two caption lines is large.

Y.note: Same template and similar polish, with a charming archival feel. The B&W photo is lower contrast, and the figure is small and washed out against the bright trees. The torn emulsion edge adds authenticity. The caption is readable, but the grey source line is small and the white mat behind the caption area reduces contrast. The subject is tiny, so the caption is needed to identify him.

why: X's larger, higher-contrast subject with a saturated backdrop reads faster and looks richer than Y's small, washed-out figure.
top_fix_for_weaker: Crop or zoom in tighter on the subject, add contrast, and make the source line larger and brighter. Also close the gap between the two caption lines.
